title: Finite products of Noetherian modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $T$ be a finite set, and for each $t\in T$ let $M_t$ be an $R$-module. Suppose every $R$-submodule of each $M_t$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then every $R$-submodule of $\prod_{t\in T}M_t$, with componentwise operations, is finitely generated. Thus a finite product of Noetherian $R$-modules is Noetherian, where a module is called Noetherian precisely when every submodule is finitely generated. The empty product is included; $R$ itself need not be Noetherian.

from.place: Local-uniformization support for arbitrary-field duality in the ancestor route: the finite quotient in ILO VI, paragraph after Proposition 3.5 and opening of 3.7(b); the Noetherian affine quotient base is supplied by finite injective ring descent. In Eakin–Nagata descent, the finite evaluation map into a power of a faithful Noetherian module detects Noetherianity of the scalar ring.
